scenes.title: El Torres on his way to the mosque
scenes.description: A press photograph, taken in 1905 by Jean du Taillis with the Agence Rol as commissioning agency, showing El Torres on his way to the mosque. The record is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: Telescopic luggage handles with plastic grips did not exist in 1905, so this handle cannot belong to the scene.

scenes.title: M. Fibiger (CNews)
scenes.description: A press photograph from November 1927 shows M. Fibiger (CNews), taken by the Agence Rol after the original photograph by the Central News photographic agency. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, and is in the public domain.
scenes.explanation: Practical visible-spectrum LEDs did not exist in 1927, so this lamp cannot belong to the scene.

scenes.title: People, Sailboat, Pier
scenes.description: A photograph from 1929 showing people, a sailboat and a pier, held by the National Library of Norway. The record does not name a photographer or a specific location.
scenes.explanation: A molded plastic wheeled cooler could not exist in 1929 because plastic coolers with wheels were not made until the 1950s.
scenes.credit: Zapffe, Peter Wessel via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: Celebration at the Exhibition and Convention Centre
scenes.description: A photograph taken on 4 June 1942 at Juhla Messukeskuksessa in Finland.
scenes.explanation: LED stage lighting fixtures did not exist in 1942; they became common only in the 2010s.

source.titleEn: Celebration at the Exhibition and Convention Centre

scenes.title: Mr Briand's Clément-Bayard automobile
scenes.description: A press photograph from 1913 by Agence Rol shows the Clément-Bayard automobile of Mr Briand, with a private chauffeur. The glass negative is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: The jerrycan is a pressed-steel or plastic fuel container that did not exist in 1913, so it cannot belong to this pre-war automobile scene.
